title: An idle autopilot tick ends after one cheap command, with no sync push, subagent or digest commit
goal: autopilot.py status --idle (or a tick-needed command) exits 0 with one line when nothing a tick acts on changed since the last tick (no runner ended, no live runner, no new draft, no open gate, no stall signal, origin/main unmoved), and the skill's tick stops there; an idle tick today runs status, sync, selfcheck, intake with the network, horizon, digest and sync --push, whose push takes the host main lock and waits behind any land's gate
notes: Theme: idle cost. Evidence: mac-fifth counted about 35 consecutive no-op manager check-ins; kb-autopilot SKILL.md steps 1-9 run at least eight commands and a sync --push per tick; kg_sync.py:790-793 takes the host main lock for every sync --push, whatever the range; a 15-minute loop is 96 ticks a day.
